hotkey.tooltip: Keyboard shortcut that opens Tiler for the focused window.

use-push-tile.tooltip: Super with an arrow key tiles the focused window as it always has, but with Tiler's gaps and reserved space. Turn this off to leave those shortcuts to Cinnamon.

center-on-window.description: Center the grid on the focused window
center-on-window.tooltip: The grid normally appears in the middle of the screen. Turn this on to have it appear over the window being tiled instead.

tile-dialogs.tooltip: Ordinary windows are always tiled. This adds dialogs such as preferences and file choosers; dialogs that cannot be resized are skipped.

tile-toolboxes.tooltip: Floating tool windows, like the ones used by image editors.

show-autotile.description: Show auto-tile actions on the grid
show-autotile.tooltip: Adds a row of arrangements to the grid that tile every window on the workspace at once: a main window beside the rest, or everything shared out equally, each newcomer halving the largest cell.

overflow-windows.tooltip: When an auto-tile arrangement has no room for a window, this says what becomes of it: left where it was, taken out of the way, or gathered around the middle of the screen.

window-gap.tooltip: Space left between two windows tiled next to each other.

edge-gap.tooltip: Space left between a tiled window and the edge of the usable screen area.

reserved-scope.tooltip: Choose whether reserved space applies to every monitor or only the primary monitor.

reserved-top.tooltip: Windows are never tiled into this area. Useful for Conky or docks that do not reserve space themselves.

reserved-bottom.tooltip: Windows are never tiled into this area. Useful for Conky or docks that do not reserve space themselves.

reserved-left.tooltip: Windows are never tiled into this area. Useful for Conky or docks that do not reserve space themselves.

reserved-right.tooltip: Windows are never tiled into this area. Useful for Conky or docks that do not reserve space themselves.

grid-1-cols.tooltip: How many columns this grid is divided into.

grid-1-rows.tooltip: How many rows this grid is divided into.

grid-1-layout.tooltip: Columns, then rows. Sizes can be given one by one to make some tracks larger than others, so 1,2,1 x 1,1 is three columns whose middle one is twice the width of its neighbors. Changing the numbers above rewrites this, and anything that cannot be read falls back to them.

grid-1-name.tooltip: What this grid is called on the grid selector. Long names are shortened to fit. Left empty, it is named after its size.

grid-1-tooltip.tooltip: Shown when hovering this grid on the selector.
